course_description:
To be effective business analysts, graduates must understand the technology platforms that support business analytics. Numerical analysis software is the core platform on which business analytics relies. Using the numerical analysis software R, this course provides students with firsthand experience of coding and programming for business analytics. Thus, the course helps to equip students for careers as business analysts by providing them with knowledge of the platforms that support business analytics.

Course Changes in Response to Previous Student Feedback

Based on students' feedback from the previous semester, this course is taught using Python to better complement the business analytics toolkit required by industry.

course_aims: The broad aim of this course is to provide students with a structured introduction to the technologies of business analytics, with a particular emphasis on the software environments used for business analytics. Students should develop a specific understanding of how these software environments are used and the key concepts in using these software environments (including some emphasis on programming concepts for business analytics). Students should develop an appreciation of how these technologies can increase the productivity of business analysts and business analytics projects, and how businesses and analysts can deploy these technologies to support their business analytics efforts.

learning_outcomes.description: Recognise and explain the role of new and emerging technologies for business analytics.
Explain the core features of the technology platforms of business analytics.
Use and apply the technologies of business analytics with a particular emphasis on open-source computing environments.
Compare and critically evaluate the different technologies and software environments used for business analytics.
Demonstrate how the technologies of business analytics can support business decision making and improve business performance.

assessment_details.title: Python Foundations Project (A1)
assessment_details.task_description: In this assignment, students apply the Python foundations taught in the first five weeks of the course to a realistic business scenario. They must write a Python script or a Jupyter notebook that uses variables, data types, functions and data structures (e.g., lists, dictionaries, loops) to process and summarise a small business dataset provided to them. Students also write a short reflection identifying which analytics technologies or tools they used, explaining why Python was chosen for this task, and noting any ethical or governance considerations relevant to handling that data. This is important because it verifies that students can connect Python's foundational building blocks to a real business purpose before the course moves into the more demanding Pandas and data-pipeline work of the second half. assessment_details.title: Python Decision Support Project (A3)
assessment_details.task_description: Students act as a lead business analyst and build an end-to-end Python solution for a realistic organisational problem. They are provided with a dataset and a broad business problem, and must apply the full range of skills developed across the course to produce outputs that support business decision-making. The final submission includes well-documented, reproducible code and a business presentation communicating their findings and recommendations to a decision-maker. This is important because it demonstrates the complete arc that business analytics companies value: translating a business problem into a technical solution and communicating the outcome as a decision, which is the core purpose of the course.
